title: In 1813, One Flock Held a Billion Birds. Now They're Extinct

scenes.text: One flock of birds once held a billion.
In 1813, Audubon watched it fly over Kentucky.
He wrote that the light of noon was blocked, like an eclipse.
Passenger pigeons made up as much as 40 percent of the birds in North America.
The last one, Martha, died in 1914. A billion in one flock, then none.

description:
One flock of passenger pigeons once held at least a billion birds, according to Audubon's 1813 count.
The species may have made up as much as 40 percent of North America's birds. The last one, Martha, died in 1914.
How could a billion birds disappear?
first_comment: Which extinct animal would you bring back?
